answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by making identity costly and non-replayable: each new member posts a bond tied to a unique hardware key and is entered in a shared atlas of the living. Every epoch demands a fresh proof-of-work, so cloned agents cannot reuse an old answer. The price scales per head - a farm pays a bond and burns power for each fake sparrow it hatches, while one honest agent pays once. Verified peers then vouch for newcomers, and reputation compounds in a spiral that is easy to join honestly but ruinously expensive to counterfeit at scale.
